# Implementation Plan: Customer Booking Flow

**Branch**: `004-customer-booking-flow` | **Date**: 2026-03-11 | **Spec**: [spec.md](spec.md)  
**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/004-customer-booking-flow/spec.md`

**Note**: This plan was generated by the `/speckit.plan` command.

## Summary

Implement the complete customer booking journey: deep-link resolution from a QR code or shared link → organization landing page → service selection → conflict-aware time slot picker → booking form with transactional Firestore write → confirmation screen. Strict clean architecture enforced: domain use cases own all business logic (slot calculation, conflict detection), the new `AppointmentRepository` is defined in the domain layer and implemented in data, and cubits are the sole presentation-layer consumers.

Two **Firestore rules blockers** must be resolved first: (1) the appointment `create`/`update` rules are missing `customerName`, `customerPhone`, and `queuePosition` in the allowed fields list, and (2) the appointment `list` permission is admin-only — customers need it for slot queries. A compound index on `serviceId` + `scheduledAt` is also required.

No automated tests are included — testing is deferred to Sprint 8.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: Dart 3.9.0+ / Flutter 3.9.0+  
**Primary Dependencies**: flutter_bloc (Cubit), GetIt + Injectable, GoRouter 17.1.0, Firebase (Auth + Firestore + Crashlytics), Talker, equatable  
**Storage**: Cloud Firestore — subcollections `organizations/{orgId}/appointments/{id}`, `organizations/{orgId}/services/{id}`, `organizations/{orgId}/working_hours/{dayOfWeek}`  
**Testing**: Deferred to Sprint 8. No test files created in this sprint.  
**Target Platform**: Android (API 21+), iOS 13+  
**Project Type**: Mobile app (Flutter)  
**Performance Goals**: Org landing page load < 2s; slot calculation < 300ms; booking write < 2s (including transaction); screen navigation < 300ms  
**Constraints**: Offline-first Firestore cached reads; domain layer framework-agnostic (zero Flutter imports); Firestore rules must be deployed before any appointment write; 7-day rolling booking window  
**Scale/Scope**: 4 new use cases, 4 new cubits, 5 new pages, 1 new repository + datasource, 3 existing repositories reused, ~20 new files

## Constitution Check

*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-check after Phase 1 design.*

| Principle | Status | Notes |
|-----------|--------|-------|
| **I. Code Quality / Clean Architecture** | ✅ PASS | `AppointmentRepository` interface in domain, impl in data. 4 use cases encapsulate all business logic. Cubits depend on use cases only — no direct repo or datasource access. Existing `OrganizationRepository`, `ServiceRepository`, `WorkingHoursRepository` reused without modification (only slug lookup method added to shared repo). |
| **II. Flexibility & Extensibility** | ✅ PASS | All new code lives in `lib/customer/booking_flow/` (domain + presentation) and `lib/shared/booking/` (data + domain). No modifications to admin features. New Injectable registrations follow existing patterns. |
| **III. Testing Standards** | ⚠️ DEFERRED | Tests are deferred to Sprint 8 per user directive ("without testing"). Documented as an explicit assumption in spec.md. This is an accepted sprint-level exception — not a principle violation. |
| **IV. UX Consistency** | ✅ PASS | Material 3 theme reused. `AppLoadingIndicator` and `AppErrorWidget` for loading/error states. Snackbar for success/error feedback. Time picker follows system conventions. All tap targets ≥ 48×48. |
| **V. Fast Delivery** | ✅ PASS | 5 user stories prioritized P1→P5, each independently demoable. Linear implementation order follows dependency chain. No gold-plating — only spec'd requirements implemented. |
| **VI. Performance Requirements** | ✅ PASS | Firestore compound index ensures efficient appointment queries. Transactional write for conflict prevention. `const` constructors throughout. Slot calculation is pure in-memory computation (< 1ms for typical schedules). |

**Post-design re-check**:
- Constitution Check still passes after Phase 1 design.
- **Critical blockers**: Firestore rules update (R-001, R-002 in research.md) + compound index (R-007) must be deployed before any data layer code can function.

**Structure Decision**: Follows existing convention — shared data/domain in `lib/shared/booking/`, customer-specific use cases and UI in `lib/customer/booking_flow/`. Domain use cases live inside the feature module since they orchestrate feature-specific logic. Shared repositories stay in `lib/shared/` since they're consumed by both admin and customer roles.
